text.arabic_uthmani: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنكُمْ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُبْصِرُونَ

words.gloss_range: opening connector that keeps the prior deathbed scene active while launching a divine proximity claim

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following independent divine subject joined to the opening connector

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) does not let 56:85 restart cold after the watching scene of 56:84. It can carry coordination, resumption, and circumstantial overlay at once, so the divine statement arrives as a connected intervention into the very scene being observed. Because it is bound directly to the nasal-weighted {{ar:نَحْنُ}} ({{tr:naḥnu}}), the transition and the explicit divine subject are heard as one compact entry.

topics.headline: opening connector keeps the deathbed scene active
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proximity claim is not detached from 56:84; it overlays and continues the watched deathbed scene.
topics.reason: The particle is a coordinating connector, and the local clause begins immediately after 56:84; the exact discourse label may be resumptive, coordinative, or circumstantial, so the topic is kept as a live range rather than one forced function.

topics.headline: connector delivers the divine subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first word does not merely connect clauses; it brings the explicit divine subject into the scene as the next audible unit.
topics.reason: The connector is proclitic on the following pronoun, so the boundary device and the subject enter together in the surface form.

topics.headline: bound sound makes the transition compact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the recited transition as a quick join into the nasal-weighted pronoun rather than a detached pause.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation follows from the bound particle plus following pronoun and does not conflict with the syntactic analysis.

words.gloss_range: explicit first-person plural pronoun anchoring the nominal clause in the divine speaker

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following comparative predicate of the nominal clause

words.prose: {{ar:نَحْنُ}} ({{tr:naḥnu}}) makes the speaker explicit before the predicate appears. The clause could have moved more anonymously, but the independent pronoun gives the divine speaker a full word-slot and makes the claim of nearness a stated relation, not an unnamed force in the scene. Its plural form keeps royal majesty and mediated agency within range, while the local discourse still anchors the subject as the divine speaker. The nasal cluster also gives the opening subject audible weight before {{ar:أَقْرَبُ}} ({{tr:aqrabu}}) arrives.

topics.headline: independent pronoun foregrounds the speaker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine nearness is claimed by an explicit speaker, not left as an abstract or anonymous proximity.
topics.reason: The word is an overt first-person plural independent pronoun, and attachment evidence makes it the subject of the nominal clause.

topics.headline: plural form keeps divine agency range open
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plural pronoun carries majesty and agency breadth without forcing the clause to name angels as the grammatical subject.
topics.reason: The surface form is plural, but the guardrail evidence identifies the discourse speaker as divine; any attendant-agency reading must remain a qualified range, not a replacement subject.

topics.headline: human watching yields to first-person divine speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a shift from the watchers' vantage in 56:84 to a divine first-person statement of an already-standing relation.
topics.reason: The clause is nominal, with the pronoun as subject and the comparative adjective as predicate, so it states a relation rather than narrating a new event.

topics.headline: nasal weight slows the opening subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the opening subject as audibly weighted before the comparative predicate arrives.
topics.reason: The sound claim is tied to the surface pronoun and its nasal consonants.

words.prose: {{ar:أَقْرَبُ}} ({{tr:aqrabu}}) is the predicate that makes the first beat a ranked relation: the divine speaker is nearer to the dying referent than the addressed witnesses are. The following {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}) and {{ar:مِنكُمْ}} ({{tr:minkum}}) keep the comparison from floating; they build a triangle of speaker, target, and outstripped observers. The root's nearness field supplies spatial language for a relation that exceeds ordinary location, while kinship and offering-nearness branches sharpen the sense that even intimate human closeness is surpassed by access to what is being surrendered. The recurrence of the {{ar:أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:aqrabu ilayhi}}) formula (50:16) reinforces intimate divine access while this ayah specializes the comparison against human witnesses, and the same root's return around the brought-near in the surah (56:11; 56:88) keeps nearness tied to rank and death-adjacent destiny. The compact comparative form gives a broad root family a focused central word with its own acoustic weight.

topics.headline: elative predicate builds a three-party comparison
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that nearness is ranked among three parties: divine speaker, dying target, and addressed observers.
topics.reason: The word is a comparative adjective and attachment evidence shows it is the predicate completed by the following target and comparator phrases.

topics.headline: adjectival form states nearness rather than approach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause asserts an existing ranked proximity, not a movement of approach or an act of bringing near.
topics.reason: The local form is an adjective-comparative predicate; causative and motion branches exist in the root family but are not the selected local form.

topics.headline: spatial grammar carries non-spatial divine access
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah uses measurable comparative grammar while the divine subject makes the nearness more than ordinary distance.
topics.reason: V4 supports nearness in place and meaning, while the local divine predication prevents reducing the claim to bodily location alone.

topics.headline: kinship and offering branches color the outstripped closeness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the root family can evoke human nearness, kinship, and devotional access, sharpening the claim that even intimate witnesses are surpassed.
topics.reason: The branches are valid in the root family, but the local comparative adjective selects nearness/access, so kinship and offering remain secondary pressure rather than direct translation sense.

topics.headline: proximity formula recalls intimate divine access
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that {{ar:أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:aqrabu ilayhi}}) participates in a Quranic proximity formula, with this ayah changing the comparator to the witnesses (50:16).
topics.reason: The rows give a concrete parallel at 50:16; the local form shares the comparative-plus-target wording while using a different comparison partner.

topics.headline: nearness joins surah rank and unseen perception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the nearness word belongs both to the ayah's unseen-proximity contrast and to a same-surah nearness network around rank and death-adjacent destiny (56:11; 56:88).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah references and the local co-occurrence with the perception verb makes unseen nearness a live structural relation.

topics.headline: common root is narrowed into a compact elative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a broad and common nearness root is locally sharpened into a compact comparative adjective at the center of the clause.
topics.reason: The local form observation identifies an adjective-comparative slot, and the sound row is tied to the same central surface word.

words.gloss_range: directional target phrase with a masculine singular suffix referring back into the deathbed scene

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: closing second-person perception verb that resumes the addressed group

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}) gives the comparative its target before the human comparator is named. The preposition points the nearness toward him rather than merely locating the speaker with him, and the preposition-plus-suffix fusion makes direction and referent one compact surface unit. The attached suffix depends on the deathbed referent already staged in 56:83-84. A soul-referent remains a possible interpretive pressure, but the guardrail evidence keeps the default target as the dying participant inferred from the scene.

topics.headline: target phrase orients the nearness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that nearness is directed toward a target, not left as a static or general closeness.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence shows the phrase is governed as the complement of the comparative predicate.

topics.headline: suffix reaches back to the deathbed referent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah depends on the previous scene for its target; the pronoun is meaningful because 56:83-84 has already staged the dying person.
topics.reason: The suffix is masculine singular and discourse-inferred; a soul reading may be discussed, but the reference evidence warns against resolving it away from the death-scene participant by default.

topics.headline: preposition and suffix are one surface unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the target is introduced as a compact unit before the witnesses enter as comparator.
topics.reason: The surface fuses the preposition and suffix, and the local order places this target phrase before the comparator phrase.

words.gloss_range: comparative phrase naming the addressed witnesses as the surpassed baseline

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: closing second-person perception verb that resumes the addressed group

words.prose: {{ar:مِنكُمْ}} ({{tr:minkum}}) completes the comparison by naming the addressed group as the baseline surpassed. The phrase does more than supply a bare than: while its required job is comparative, it still distinguishes divine nearness from the human side marked by the preposition. It pulls the witnesses from 56:84 into the grammar of 56:85 and embeds them as the party less near to the dying person than the divine speaker. The same second-person group will then reappear inside {{ar:تُبْصِرُونَ}} ({{tr:tubṣirūna}}), first as outstripped comparator and then as failed perceivers.

topics.headline: human witnesses become the surpassed comparator
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the witnesses are not merely nearby; they are grammatically made the baseline that divine nearness exceeds.
topics.reason: The phrase is the comparison complement of the elative predicate and supplies the explicit party being outstripped.

topics.headline: comparison keeps a separation undertone
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparator phrase can still feel like a distinction from the human side, even though its required local job is comparative.
topics.reason: The local grammar requires comparison after the elative; source or partitive undertones may color the phrase but should not replace the comparative function.

topics.headline: second-person group carries through the ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same watchers are carried from the previous verse into the comparison and then into the closing verb.
topics.reason: The suffix is second-person plural and the closing verb also carries second-person plural agreement.

words.gloss_range: connector fused to the adversative particle, linking the proximity claim to the perception denial

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following adversative particle joined to the connector
local adversative-plus-negator sequence whose repeated onset creates the cadence

words.prose: The second {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) has a different job from the opening connector. Attached to {{ar:لَٰكِنْ}} ({{tr:lākin}}), it does not merely add another statement; it carries the first beat into an adversative turn. The result is a connected correction: divine nearness is asserted, and then the same clause-complex turns toward the observers' non-perception. The sequence into {{ar:لَٰكِنْ لَّا}} ({{tr:lākin lā}}) also repeats the la onset, making the turn toward negation audible before the final verb names the failure.

topics.headline: connector supports the adversative hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial of perception answers the nearness claim directly rather than beginning as an isolated comment.
topics.reason: The connector is immediately attached to the adversative particle, and clause evidence identifies the second clause as a contrast with the nearness statement.

topics.headline: repetition does not mean identical function
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the two connectors in the ayah are shaped by their neighbors: the first opens the declaration, while this one carries the correction.
topics.reason: The same particle occurs twice, but this occurrence is fused with the adversative particle and therefore functions inside the contrastive turn.

topics.headline: repeated onset makes the turn audible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the audible turn into negation before the final perception verb names the failure.
topics.reason: The sound observation is tied to the adjacent surface sequence of adversative particle and negator.

words.gloss_range: light adversative particle introducing the negated verbal sentence as a correction to expected visibility

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: negated verbal sentence introduced by the light adversative particle

words.prose: {{ar:لَٰكِنْ}} ({{tr:lākin}}) is the hinge between the two beats. As the light adversative particle, it introduces the verbal sentence {{ar:لَّا تُبْصِرُونَ}} ({{tr:lā tubṣirūna}}) without governing a following noun, so the verse moves straight from proximity to negated perception. Its correction does not cancel the first claim; it blocks the expected inference that real nearness must be visible to the observers.

topics.headline: light particle opens a verbal sentence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle does not restructure the clause with noun governance; it sends the line directly into the negated verb.
topics.reason: The local form is the light adversative particle before a negated verbal sentence, not the heavy noun-governing form.

topics.headline: adversative keeps nearness and non-sight together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the paradox: divine nearness remains true precisely where the observers' sight fails.
topics.reason: Clause evidence marks the second clause as contrastive with the first, preserving the nearness claim while introducing non-perception.

words.gloss_range: simple negator immediately scoping over the following imperfect perception verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following imperfect perception verb directly negated by the particle

words.prose: {{ar:لَّا}} ({{tr:lā}}) places the denial exactly on {{ar:تُبْصِرُونَ}} ({{tr:tubṣirūna}}), not on the prior claim of nearness. Because it is simple negation with an indicative imperfect, it reports present, habitual, or broader non-perception without becoming a prohibition or a past-only denial. The particle therefore makes the problem seeing itself: the nearness stands, but the observers do not perceive it. Its compressed doubled-lām shape gives the denial audible pressure at the start of the final phrase.

topics.headline: simple negation leaves non-perception temporally open
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial is neither a command nor a past-only report; it remains present, habitual, or broadly applicable.
topics.reason: The negator precedes an indicative imperfect verb, which rules out prohibitive or jussive governance.

topics.headline: negation targets seeing, not nearness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse denies the addressees' perception of the nearness, not the nearness itself.
topics.reason: Translation support explicitly preserves the negation scope over the following verb after the adversative particle.

topics.headline: non-sight may be situational or constitutive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the observers' failure can be read as the immediate scene's non-perception and as a broader inability to register this kind of hidden nearness.
topics.reason: The local form leaves temporal and habitual scope open, but it does not force a metaphysical incapacity as the only reading.

topics.headline: compressed negator foregrounds denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the denial as audibly prominent at the start of the final phrase.
topics.reason: The sound claim is tied to the written doubled form of the negator immediately before the perception verb.

words.gloss_range: negated Form IV imperfect of seeing or discerning, with second-person plural subject and no overt object
words.root_gloss_range: broad sight and insight family including eye-seeing, inner discernment, clarification, and unrelated concrete branches; the local form selects active perception or perceptual capacity under negation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following imperfect perception verb directly negated by the particle

words.prose: {{ar:تُبْصِرُونَ}} ({{tr:tubṣirūna}}) makes the closing failure active and direct: the addressed group itself is the subject of non-perception. The imperfect keeps the failure present or ongoing, and the missing object leaves the unseen field open rather than naming only one target. As a Form IV finite verb, it names perception or perceptual capacity, not seeking insight, reflective consideration, or an external act of making someone see. Since the root covers seeing and discernment, the ayah denies more than optical registration; the watchers look at the deathbed scene but do not perceive the hidden nearness and agency that the verse has just asserted. The final word also answers the looking of 56:84, resonates with the contrastive formula in 2:154, where hidden death-related reality is likewise not perceived through the human channel named there, and sets denied human sight against the wider Quranic field of divine seeing. Its emphatic center and long plural ending make the closing diagnosis firm and weighty in sound.

topics.headline: imperfect indicative keeps failure ongoing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the failure is not confined to a completed missed sighting; it remains present, habitual, or ongoing.
topics.reason: The verb is imperfect indicative under simple negation, retaining the indicative plural ending.

topics.headline: verb ending puts the audience inside the failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressed witnesses are not merely mentioned earlier; their own verb form carries the indictment.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the verb's subject agreement as second-person masculine plural, matching the addressed group in the comparator phrase.

topics.headline: objectless perception leaves the unseen target open
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse refuses to name a single object of sight, leaving divine nearness, the death process, and hidden agency within the denied perceptual field.
topics.reason: The verb instance has no overt object, and the valency profile supports objectless uses; the topic is narrowed because no one unseen target should be supplied as the only object.

topics.headline: the denied channel is visual discernment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the failure is framed through sight and discernment, not generic ignorance or mere feeling.
topics.reason: V4 supports eye-seeing and inner insight as central branches of the root, and the local verb chooses that channel for the denied act or capacity.

topics.headline: nearby family forms are not the local form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse names basic perception or capacity, not seeking insight, reflective consideration, or an external act of making someone see.
topics.reason: The root family contains related insight and causative forms, but the local surface is Form IV imperfect, so those branches sharpen by contrast rather than supply the direct sense.

topics.headline: common root is narrowed into Form IV finite use
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a broad sight root is locally focused into an active Form IV perception event or capacity under negation.
topics.reason: The local form observation identifies Form IV, and the CRITICAL distribution rows argue for form-sensitive reading rather than an undifferentiated root gloss.

topics.headline: parallel formula shifts from sensing to seeing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a death-related hiddenness formula where this ayah uses sight-discernment while 2:154 uses sensory awareness.
topics.reason: The rows give the concrete reference 2:154 and identify the structural contrast between the two perception channels.

topics.headline: 56:84 looking becomes 56:85 non-seeing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the watchers' looking in 56:84 is answered by a stronger diagnosis of failed sight-discernment in 56:85.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the concrete boundary relation to 56:84 and distinguish directed looking from true perception.

topics.headline: human non-seeing resonates with divine seeing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an asymmetry between denied human perception and the broader Quranic field of divine seeing.
topics.reason: The echo rows connect the same root to divine seeing language; this is a resonance, not a claim that a divine title is locally present.

topics.headline: human vantage is corrected by divine speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same deathbed moment rotating from human observation to divine disclosure of unseen nearness.
topics.reason: The root-pair and boundary rows match the ayah's structure: nearness is asserted from divine speech while human perception is negated.

topics.headline: closing verb makes failed perception the landing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah's final semantic and audible landing is the audience's inability to perceive the nearness just asserted.
topics.reason: The verb is verse-final and gathers the negation, root-pair contrast, and clause architecture into the final word.

topics.headline: final sound gives weight to the failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final verb as a firm, weighty recitational close rather than a light ending.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows are tied to the final verb's emphatic consonant and plural ending.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction أَقْرَبُ ... مِنكُمْ ... لَا تُبْصِرُونَ directly couples comparative nearness with negated visual perception.
baseline_models.mechanism: Spatial or relational distance and perceptual access are decoupled: the nearer party can be immediately present while the more distant observers' eyes do not register it.

activation_trace.role: Nearness as the opposite of distance supplies the comparative spatial or relational arrangement.
Eyesight supplies the denied sensory channel, making invisibility compatible with immediate presence.

changed_reading.before: Nearness would ordinarily make a presence easier for the addressed observers to see.
changed_reading.after: The ayah asserts a presence nearer to the person than the observers are precisely while denying those observers visual access to it.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Negated تُبْصِرُونَ can activate the ب ص ر branch of inward discernment alongside the comparative أَقْرَبُ.
baseline_models.mechanism: Closeness is not sufficient for recognition: a reality may already be intimately available while the addressed group lacks the inward penetration needed to apprehend it.

activation_trace.role: Nearness supplies immediate availability rather than remoteness.
Insight and verified knowledge turn the negation from an optical failure into failed recognition.

changed_reading.before: You do not visually see a nearby presence.
changed_reading.after: You do not penetrate or recognize a reality that is already closer to the person than you are.

context_deltas.mechanism: The concealed record and its restricted contact provide an access-control analogue: something can be present and consequential while remaining enclosed from an unqualified mode of contact. The focus contrast then reads as near reality behind an access boundary, not reality at a great distance.

activation_trace.role: Immediate nearness prevents concealment from being reduced to spatial remoteness.
Inward discernment supplies the unavailable mode of access.
Protective concealment supplies an enclosure that preserves a thing while withholding ordinary access.
Touch by hand supplies the concrete access operation that the sequence restricts.
Purity as removal of defilement supplies the qualification for crossing the access boundary.

structural_cues: The pre-focus sequence places a concealed book immediately beside a statement that only a qualified group touches it.
The focus ayah repeats the same paradoxical geometry: nearness without ordinary access.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies concealment, restricted touch, qualification, and near-but-unperceived presence; I infer one access-boundary pattern across them. A live alternative is that the book sequence and death scene use separate kinds of concealment.

changed_reading.before: The observers simply fail to notice a nearby presence.
changed_reading.after: The observers face a reality that is near but enclosed behind a mode-of-access boundary their present sight does not cross.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding progression fixes the focus at a terminal bodily threshold: something reaches the throat while the companions are actively looking. Nearness therefore becomes operational proximity to the transition itself, whereas human looking reaches only its visible bodily surface.

activation_trace.role: Approaching and coming into immediate contact recasts nearness as involvement at the threshold.
Eyesight is the channel explicitly unable to register the nearer operation.
Arrival at an endpoint supplies the terminal movement into the scene.
The throat as the passage of food and breath locates the endpoint at a bodily conduit.
Directed looking supplies deliberate eyewitness attention, sharpening the contrast with failure to perceive.

structural_cues: 56:83 gives arrival at the throat, 56:84 gives the companions' looking, and 56:85 interrupts that visible scene with a nearer unseen party.
The comparative مِنكُمْ places the nearer party and the human observers around the same person.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies endpoint, throat passage, active looking, and comparative nearness; I infer that the unseen party has operational access to the transition itself. The alternative is purely spatial proximity without an asserted causal role.

changed_reading.before: An unseen party is spatially closer than the visible companions.
changed_reading.after: At the exact bodily threshold the companions watch, the nearer party occupies the operative side of the transition while human sight remains at its exterior.

context_deltas.mechanism: The challenge after the focus converts comparative nearness into a test of effective authority: those who deny being subject to reckoning are invited to reverse the passage, but cannot. The nearer position thus carries jurisdiction over an event the visible companions cannot control.

activation_trace.role: Privileged nearness to authority supplies an ordered relation rather than mere metric distance.
Failure of discernment explains why the addressed group mistakes lack of visible control for lack of governing authority.
Reckoning and recompense supply the jurisdiction explicitly placed in question.
Returning something to its former state supplies the demanded reversal that tests control.
Fulfilling a claim in action makes successful reversal the proof demanded from the challengers.

structural_cues: The two following ayat form a conditional challenge: if the observers are outside judgment, they should return what has reached the throat.
The second-person plural continues the group addressed by مِنكُمْ and لَا تُبْصِرُونَ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies denied reckoning, a demand for reversal, and a truth test; I infer that the nearer party's proximity entails effective jurisdiction over the transition. Alternatively, the challenge may establish power generally without defining the semantic content of nearness.

changed_reading.before: The comparative describes who is closest to the person.
changed_reading.after: The comparative also distinguishes effective jurisdiction: the unseen nearer party governs the passage that the visible companions cannot reverse.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate reuse of ق ر ب in الْمُقَرَّبِينَ changes nearness from a momentary relation around the dying person into a possible conferred status beyond the threshold. The nearer presence and the brought-near destination-category remain distinct, but the lexical echo makes proximity directional and rank-bearing.

activation_trace.role: Comparative nearness supplies the relation first stated at the threshold.
The favored brought-near group supplies a ranked and conferred form of proximity after the threshold.

structural_cues: After the return challenge, the passage immediately sorts the person into outcomes beginning with الْمُقَرَّبِينَ.
The same root shifts from the active comparison أَقْرَبُ to the passive status مُقَرَّبِينَ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a comparative q-r-b form followed by a passive brought-near q-r-b category; I infer that threshold nearness foreshadows conferred rank or destination. The live alternative is lexical recurrence without identity between the nearer party and the classified person.

changed_reading.before: Nearness names only the unseen party's position during the death scene.
changed_reading.after: Nearness also opens toward a conferred post-threshold rank: the scene of who is nearer is followed by the possibility of the person being brought near.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing assertion of reality and settled knowledge prevents لَا تُبْصِرُونَ from functioning as an epistemic veto. Sensory nonappearance marks a limit of the observers' present mode, while the event is framed as fixed reality and certainty.

activation_trace.role: Denied eyesight supplies the limited evidentiary mode whose failure is being contained.
Insight supplies a broader apprehension not exhausted by immediate optical evidence.
Reality fixed against falsehood supplies the ontic status unaffected by nonappearance.
Stable knowledge with doubt removed supplies the epistemic endpoint beyond present sight.

structural_cues: The passage closes its outcome sequence with حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ after the earlier denial of visual perception.
The demonstrative هَٰذَا gathers the narrated transition and outcomes as the object of the certainty claim.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies sensory denial followed by fixed reality and doubtless knowledge; I infer that the perception gap is mode-specific rather than evidence of absence. Alternatively, the closing certainty may confirm the whole outcome sequence without targeting 56:85 in particular.

changed_reading.before: What the observers cannot see remains epistemically inaccessible.
changed_reading.after: Their inability to see identifies a bounded sensory mode; it does not diminish the passage's claim that the unseen transition is fixed reality.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the birth-nearness branch of ق ر ب and the fetus branch of ج ن ن across surfaces that ordinarily denote comparative nearness and a garden. It remains anchored in أَقْرَبُ and in the packet's throat-to-spirit sequence, which together support a threshold analogy. Downstream prose should present it only as an exploratory inverse-birth image, not as the lexical meaning of the ayah or of جَنَّة.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus أَقْرَبُ can activate nearness of birth, while the immediately surrounding sequence locates a life-ending passage at the throat.

activation_trace.role: Nearness of birth turns comparative closeness into imminence at a bodily passage.
The throat as food-and-breath conduit supplies the bodily threshold for the inverse-birth analogy.
Spirit or life supplies what can be imagined as emerging through the terminal threshold.
The hidden fetus branch supplies the cross-domain image of emergence from one enclosed mode into another.

changed_reading.before: The nearer unseen presence attends an ending that the companions cannot perceive.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the ending can be imaged as an inverse birth: life crosses a throat-threshold into a hidden mode while the nearer presence attends the passage.

strongest_changes: The throat-and-looking sequence revises generic nearness into operational access at a terminal bodily threshold.
The return challenge recasts nearness as effective jurisdiction that visible companions cannot match.
The later مُقَرَّبِينَ echo extends nearness from threshold position toward conferred rank.
حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ makes failed eyesight a bounded mode of access rather than evidence of absence.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah becomes a hinge between two access regimes: companions can look at the visible body but cannot reach the nearer operation, while the passage moves from concealed text through a concealed transition to classified outcomes and certainty.
remaining_uncertainties: The comparative nearness may be spatial, relational, operational, or several of these at once.
The concealed-book sequence may genuinely prime the death scene's access boundary or may remain only a useful structural analogy.
The link from أَقْرَبُ to مُقَرَّبِينَ is lexically strong but does not by itself identify the nearer party with the brought-near person.
The inverse-birth model depends on branch-distant activation and should remain exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Causal nearness hidden inside visible distance.** `ق ر ب` **B001** supplies nearness opposite distance; `ب ص ر` **B001** supplies seeing with the eye, here negated. The observers are physically present, yet the speaker claims greater nearness. **Abductive move:** I infer that the comparison concerns effective access or agency rather than measurable bodily distance. **Reading change:** proximity is redefined by causal reach.

2. **Privileged access exceeds inner sight.** `ق ر ب` **B004** supplies access and privileged nearness; `ب ص ر` **B002** supplies inner sight. Its negation contrasts sharply with the earlier `المقربون`. **Abductive move:** I infer that those watching lack the perceptual access corresponding to the speaker’s nearness. **Reading change:** the ayah exposes an invisible hierarchy of access at death.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The `مقربين` classification at 56:88 made nearness reciprocal but asymmetric: the speaker has effective access, while selected persons are granted it.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Causal nearness exceeds bodily proximity and remains outside the witnesses’ visual capacity.** Comparative `ق ر ب` (B001, nearness as the opposite of distance) places the speaker nearer than the onlookers, while negated `ب ص ر` (B001, seeing with the eye; B002, inner sight and verification) denies their apprehension. Ayat 80–84 move from lordly descent to the watched throat-limit; ayat 86–90 test exemption and reversal, then reopen the brought-near and right-hand classes. The packet supplies comparative proximity plus failed sight; I infer that nearness here is operative access, not measurable crowding around the body. The line corrects the assumption that the closest visible human is the most causally present.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 56:88 reuses `ق ر ب` in the passive brought-near designation, revealing that the operative nearness hidden from observers can become privileged relational access when conferred.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi insanların veya hayvanların suya varış yaklaşınca geceleyin aceleyle su kaynağına yönelmesini ve bu yolculuğun gecesini anlatır. Suyu arayan kişi veya hayvan da aynı amaçlı hareketten adlandırılır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, gece yürüyüşünü yalnız suya ulaşma amacı ve yaklaşan sulama vaktiyle birlikte kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Suya gece yönelme olayı, bu gecenin adı ve su arayan varlık ayrı sözlüksel yapılarda tutulur; genel gece yolculuğuna genişletilmez.

concept_map.definition: İnsanların veya hayvanların suya varış vakti yaklaşınca geceleyin hızlanarak su kaynağına yönelmesidir. Bu yolculuğun gecesi ve gece su arayan varlık da aynı olaydan adlandırılır.

facets.statement: Topluluk veya hayvanlar, ertesi gün suya varmak üzere geceleyin su kaynağına doğru yürür.
Suya varış yaklaşınca yürüyüş hızlanabilir ve hayvanlar kaynağa doğru sertçe sürülebilir.
Gece su arayan kişi veya hayvan ile bu yolculuğun gecesi olaydan türeyen adlarla belirtilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar suya varıştan önceki gece yürüyüşünü, kaynağa doğru acele ettirmeyi ve su arayan varlığı ortak bir olay çevresinde birleştirir.

concept_gloss.text: geceleyin su kaynağına yönelme
concept_gloss.applicability: Yolculuğun zamanını, suya ulaşma amacını ve kaynağa yaklaşma hareketini birlikte karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Gece yürüyüşünü, su arama amacını, acele etmeyi ve olaydan türeyen adlandırmaları korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İnsan veya hayvan topluluğunun ertesi günkü suya varış için gece yol aldığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Gece hareketini ve suya ulaşma amacını açık biçimde korur.
error_profile.loses: Acele ettirme ile su arayan varlık ve yolculuk gecesinin adlarını dışarıda bırakır.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalın çekirdeğinde geceleyin yol alma bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalda suya ulaşma amacı ve yaklaşan varış nedeniyle hızlanma kurucudur; komşu dalda gece yolculuğunun amacı sınırlı değildir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه سير القوم والإبل نحو الماء عند قرب الورد وليلة القرب والقارب طالب الماء ليلا والعجلة والسوق الشديد إلى المورد

branches.source_phrase_ar: من الباب القرب وهي ليلة ورود الإبل الماء والقارب الطالب الماء ليلا (maqayis)؛ القرب أن يرعى القوم بينهم وبين المورد حتى إذا كان بينهم وبين الماء عشية أو ليلة عجلوا فقربوا وحمار قارب يطلب الماء (ayn)؛ قربت الإبل الماء إذا طلبته وليلة القرب ليلة طلب الماء (jamhara)؛ القرب سير الليل لورد الغد والقارب طالب الماء ليلا (sihah)؛ ليلة القرب هو السوق الشديد وتقرب أي اعجل وقربت الماء أي طلبته والقرب سير الليل (tahdhib)؛ رجل قارب قرب من الماء وليلة القرب وأقربوا إبلهم (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi su çekmek ve taşımak için kullanılan bilinen deri su kabını açıkça adlandırır. Su arama gecesi, kılıç kabı ve doluluğa yaklaşma anlamları bu nesne kimliğine dahil değildir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Tanım su almaya yarayan su tulumuyla sınırlıdır; başka kaplar ve suya gitme olayı ayrı tutulur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak dal yalnız su çekilen ve taşınan su tulumunu tanımlar; başka kalıplaşmış yakınlık anlamları içeri alınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Kuyudan veya başka bir kaynaktan su çekmek ve su taşımak için kullanılan, çoğunlukla deriden yapılmış su tulumudur.

facets.statement: Nesne su çekmek ve taşımak için kullanılan bir su kabıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar sözcüğü su çekmeye yarayan bilinen bir su tulumu olarak ortak biçimde tanımlar ve tekil ile çoğul biçimlerini kaydeder.

concept_gloss.text: su tulumu
concept_gloss.applicability: Su çekme ve taşıma işlevli kabı doğal ve doğrudan karşılayan Türkçe addır.

error_profile.preserves: Kabın su için kullanılmasını ve tulum türü bir taşıma kabı olmasını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Nesnenin biçim ve kullanımını tanımayan okur için açıklayıcı karşılık olarak kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Nesnenin kap oluşunu, su taşıma işlevini ve yaygın deri malzemesini korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal genel olarak su çekip taşımaya yarayan su tulumunu adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal büyük, parçaları birleştirilmiş veya eskidiğinde su sızdırabilen özel bir su kabını da adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da sıvı, özellikle su taşımaya yarayan deri kap bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal işlev bakımından genel su tulumudur; komşu dal biçimi, büyüklüğü veya birleşik yapısıyla belirlenen ayrı bir kap türüdür.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; aynı kap alanındaki özel büyük veya birleşik su kabı en yararlı sınır karşılaştırmasını sağlar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kılıç veya bıçağın içinde taşındığı kabı ortaklaştırır, fakat bunun doğrudan kın mı yoksa kının üstündeki deri dış kap mı olduğu konusunda iki sınır verir. Dal korunabilir, ancak bu nesne farkı tanımda açık bırakılmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Kavram kılıç veya bıçak kabıdır; bazı kullanımlarda kının kendisini, bazılarında kını saran dış deri kabı belirtir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Kılıç kabı adı ile kılıcı bu kaba koyma yapısı birlikte korunur; su tulumuna veya genel kap anlamına genişletilmez.

concept_map.definition: Kılıç veya bıçağın taşındığı kın ya da kını ve askısını çevreleyen deri dış kaptır. Aynı söz alanı, kılıcı bu kaba koyma işlemini de anlatır.

facets.statement: Nesne kılıç veya bıçağı içinde taşıyan kap ya da kını çevreleyen deri dış kaptır.
Kılıcı kaba yerleştirmek veya ona bir kap sağlamak aynı sözlüksel alandaki eylem kullanımıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar kılıç veya bıçak için bir taşıma kabında birleşir; kabın doğrudan kın mı yoksa kının üzerindeki deri dışlık mı sayılacağı konusunda iki açıklama sunar ve kılıcı kaba koyma eylemini de kaydeder.

concept_gloss.text: kılıç kını veya deri dış kabı
concept_gloss.applicability: Kaynaklardaki kın ile kının dışındaki deri kap ayrımını silmeden nesnenin ortak işlevini karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Kılıç kabı işlevini ve kın ile dış deri kap arasındaki kaynak değişkenliğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kın ile dış deri kap ayrımının bağlamda önemli olmadığı genel anlatımlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Nesnenin kılıcı taşıyan ve koruyan kap işlevini korur.
error_profile.loses: Kabın bazı tanıklıklarda kının kendisi, bazılarında ise kının dışındaki deri parça olması ayrımını belirsiz bırakır.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da kılıcın taşındığı deri bir koruyucu kabı anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal kılıca doğrudan bağlı kın veya dış kın alanındadır; komşu dal kınlı kılıcı başka araçlarla birlikte alabilen daha geniş bir taşıma çantasıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi büyük deniz gemilerinin yanında bulunan, onları izleyen veya kısa işler için kullanılan küçük tekneyi açıkça tanımlar. Gece su arayan kişiyle eşseslilik, nesnenin kimliğine dahil değildir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, büyük gemiye bağlı veya onun hizmetinde kullanılan küçük tekneyle sınırlıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak dal küçük hizmet teknesini tanımlar; su arayan kişi anlamı veya genel gemi adı içeri alınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Büyük deniz gemisinin yanında bulunan, onu izleyen veya gemidekilerin kısa süreli işleri için kullanılan küçük teknedir.

facets.statement: Küçük tekne büyük bir deniz gemisine eşlik eder ve gemidekilerin kısa işleri için kullanılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar nesneyi büyük deniz gemisine eşlik eden ve gemi sahiplerinin işleri için kullanılan küçük tekne olarak ortak biçimde tanımlar.

concept_gloss.text: gemiye bağlı küçük hizmet teknesi
concept_gloss.applicability: Küçüklüğü, ana gemiyle ilişkisini ve hizmet işlevini birlikte karşılayan açıklamadır.

error_profile.preserves: Küçük tekne olmayı, büyük gemiye eşlik etmeyi ve kısa işlerde kullanılmayı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Ana gemiye bağlı küçük teknenin hizmet veya kısa ulaşım amacıyla kullanıldığı bağlamlarda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Ana gemide taşınabilen veya ona bağlı küçük tekne düşüncesini korur.
error_profile.adds: Modern kullanımda özellikle can kurtarma işlevini çağrıştırabilir; kaynak çekirdeğinde bu işlev zorunlu değildir.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da küçük bir tekne türünü anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın kimliği ana gemiyle işlevsel bağlılığa dayanır; komşu dal ise bu ilişkiyi gerektirmeyen genel bir küçük tekne adıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi doğumu yaklaşmış gebe dişiyi ortaklaştırır ve koyun, kısrak, kadın ile dişi eşek örneklerini verir. Bununla birlikte bazı tanıklıklar aynı adlandırmayı deve için kullanmamayı özellikle belirttiğinden tanım bütün gebe hayvanlara sınırsızca genellenemez.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Yaklaşan doğum kurucudur; sözlüksel adlandırmanın deveye uygulanması tanıklıklarda açıkça sınırlandırılır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Doğumu yaklaşma olayı ile bu durumdaki dişinin adı birlikte korunur; yapı bütün hayvan türlerine genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Koyun, kısrak, kadın veya dişi eşek gibi gebe bir dişinin doğum vaktinin yaklaşması ya da bu durumdaki dişidir. Bazı tanıklıklarda aynı adlandırmanın deve için kullanılmadığı belirtilir.

facets.statement: Gebe dişinin doğum veya yavrulama vakti yaklaşmıştır.
Adlandırma koyun, kısrak, kadın ve dişi eşek için tanıklanırken bazı tanıklıklarda deve kapsam dışında tutulur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar doğumu yaklaşmış gebe dişide birleşir; tür örnekleri koyun, kısrak, kadın ve dişi eşeğe uzanır, deve içinse açık bir kullanım sınırlaması bildirilir.

concept_gloss.text: doğumu yaklaşmış gebe dişi
concept_gloss.applicability: Yaklaşan doğum evresini ve bu evredeki dişiyi birlikte karşılar; tür sınırlaması ayrıca belirtilmelidir.

error_profile.preserves: Gebeliği, doğumun yaklaşmasını ve dişi katılımcıyı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Koyun, kısrak, kadın veya dişi eşeğin doğum vaktinin yakın olduğunu bildiren cümlelerde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Doğum vaktinin yaklaşması olayını doğal bir fiil yapısıyla korur.
error_profile.loses: Bu durumdaki dişiyi adlandıran isim kullanımını ve deveye ilişkin sözlüksel sınırlamayı tek başına göstermez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal belirli sözlüksel biçimi koyun, kısrak, kadın ve dişi eşek için tanıklar, bazı tanıklıklarda deveyi dışlar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal doğumu yaklaşmış gebe varlığı daha genel biçimde anlatır ve deveyi de açıkça kapsayabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da gebe dişinin doğum veya yavrulama vaktinin yaklaşmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Olay çekirdeği ortaktır; ayrım, odak daldaki tarihsel sözlüksel biçimin türlere göre sınırlı dağılım göstermesidir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; ortak olay çekirdeğine rağmen deve kapsamındaki farkı gösteren bu komşu en yararlı karşılaştırmadır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi atın yakında tutulup gözetilmesini, hazırlanmasını ve değer verilerek başıboş bırakılmamasını; develerin ise binmek için bağlanıp eyerlenmesini anlatır. Doğumun yaklaşması bu hayvan niteliğinin parçası değildir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnız hazırlanıp yakında tutulan binek hayvanlarına özgü adlandırmaları kapsar; genel hayvan veya gebelik adı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam yalnız at ve deveyle kurulan özel ad öbeklerinde geçerlidir; çıplak köke genel bir binek anlamı yüklenmez.

concept_map.definition: Atın kullanılmaya hazır biçimde yakında tutulup gözetilmesi ve değer verilerek başıboş bırakılmaması ya da develerin binmek için bağlanıp eyerlenmiş olmasıdır.

facets.statement: At kullanılmaya hazır biçimde yakında tutulur, gözetilir ve değer verilerek başıboş bırakılmaz.
Develer binmek amacıyla bağlanmış, donatılmış veya üzerlerine eyer konmuş durumda olabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar at için yakında tutma, hazırlama ve değer verme özelliklerini birleştirir; deve kullanımında ise binmek üzere bağlama ve eyerleme öne çıkar.

concept_gloss.text: yakında tutulan ve binmeye hazırlanan hayvan
concept_gloss.applicability: Atla ilgili gözetme ve hazırlığı, deveyle ilgili bağlama ve eyerlemeyi ortak binek işlevinde birleştirir.

error_profile.preserves: Yakında tutmayı, değer vermeyi, hazırlamayı ve binme amacını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: At veya devenin yakın yerde hazır ve donatılmış durumda tutulduğu bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Binek hayvanının kullanılmaya hazır ve yakın tutulması özelliklerini korur.
error_profile.loses: Atın özellikle değer görüp başıboş bırakılmaması ile devenin bağlanıp eyerlenmesi ayrıntılarını birleştirir.
